title: Fernway docs audit
lede: Every README, changelog, API reference and guide across the Fernway repos, checked against the 3.0.2 code and release notes. Most of what's stale is one story: the docs still describe 2.x, before 3.0 renamed the package, renumbered the rules and made strict mode the default.

good.label: current
good.means: matches the code and the release notes

watch.label: unverifiable
watch.means: nothing in the repo can confirm it

problem.label: stale
problem.means: contradicted by the code or the release notes

out.label: flag only
out.means: a dated record; noted, not edited

grid.title: Every doc, by status
grid.lede: One row per repo or site, one column per kind of doc. Hover a cell for what it found; click it to jump to the detail.

kinds.title: Findings by kind
kinds.lede: Every finding per row, split by what is wrong. The bars share one scale.

details.title: Detail, row by row
details.lede: Every finding, with the doc's line, what it says, and the fix written as current state.

grid.cell_note: A number is how many claims in that doc are at the cell's status. Sign-off cells show where the maintainer review stands instead.

readme.tip: Old package name, old import path, old minimum Python

changelog.tip: One release date is wrong; release entries are records

api.tip: Caching and thread-safety claims have no test

guides.label: validation rules
guides.tip: Three rule tables use the 2.x numbering

detail.summary: The README and the rules guide still describe 2.x. The changelog's one error sits in a dated entry, so it's flagged and left as written.

rows: `pip install fernway`; the package was renamed in 2.0.
`from fernway import check`; 3.0 folded the submodule into the package.

blocks.title: Guide: validation rules

image.alt: Bar chart of rule codes in the guide that don't match the code: core 0 of 12, numeric 3 of 9, text 3 of 8, dates 5 of 9.
image.caption: Codes per module that differ from `RULES` in `fernway/rules.py`.

blocks.story: Three of the guide's four rule tables use the 2.x numbering. The dates module moved the most: five of its nine codes changed when 3.0 split date rules from time rules. The core table is still right.

blocks.title: API reference
blocks.story: Two claims can't be checked from the code or the release notes: that `Schema.compile` caches its result, and that `check` is thread-safe. Neither has a test behind it.

blocks.title: Guide: migrating to 3.0
blocks.story: It promises that 2.x config files load unchanged. No test loads a 2.x config, so the promise can't be confirmed either way.

blocks.title: `CHANGELOG.md`
blocks.story: The 2.4.0 entry is dated 2023-03-14, a week before its tag. Release entries are records, so this is flagged and not edited.

api.tip: Documents --strict and the removed lint command

detail.summary: The command reference predates 3.0's switch to strict mode by default.

blocks.title: Command reference

image.alt: Terminal output of fernway check --help listing --lenient, --rules, --format and --help, with no --strict option.
image.caption: `fernway check --help` at 3.0.2. The option list has no `--strict`.

blocks.story: The reference still documents the 2.x flags. At 3.0 strict mode became the default, `--lenient` replaced `--strict`, and `lint` folded into `check`.

rows: Pass `--strict` to fail on any rule error.
Strict is the default; pass `--lenient` to report failures as warnings.

blocks.title: Guide: shell completion
blocks.story: It installs completion with `fernway completion install`, which 3.0 replaced with the standard `--install-completion` option.

blocks.story: It tells readers to install `fernway<3` before running the notebooks. The notebooks import 3.0 names, so that pin breaks every one of them.

top.title: The install line names a package that no longer exists
top.says: Both the README and the tutorial tell new users to `pip install fernway-validate`.
top.evidence: `pyproject.toml` names the package `fernway`. `fernway-validate` was last published as 1.9.4, so a new user installs a two-year-old release.
top.fix: Change the install line to `pip install fernway`.
top.where: Fixed in the docs PR for fernway; the site picks it up on its next build.

top.title: The rules guide uses the 2.x rule codes
top.says: Eleven of the 38 rule codes in the validation-rules guide are the numbers rules had before 3.0.
top.evidence: Compared code by code with `RULES` in `fernway/rules.py`; the dates module drifted most.

image.alt: Bar chart of rule codes in the guide that don't match the code: core 0 of 12, numeric 3 of 9, text 3 of 8, dates 5 of 9.

top.fix: Regenerate the three stale tables from `RULES`, and add a docs check that fails when they drift.
top.where: Fixed in the docs PR for fernway; the drift check is a separate PR.

top.title: Five API pages link to a removed module
top.says: Five API reference pages link to `fernway.legacy`, which 3.0 removed.
top.evidence: Each link returns a 404 on the built site.
top.fix: Point the links at `fernway.compat` and `fernway.RULES`, which replaced it.
top.where: Flagged to the site maintainers. The pages come from docstrings in fernway, so the fix lands there.

top.title: The CLI docs still show `--strict`
top.says: The command reference tells users to pass `--strict` to fail on rule errors.
top.evidence: 3.0 made strict mode the default and replaced the flag with `--lenient`; the help output has no `--strict`.

image.alt: Terminal output of fernway check --help with no --strict option.

top.fix: Say strict is the default, and document `--lenient` for warnings only.
top.where: Fixed in the docs PR for fernway-cli.

top.title: The migration guide promises 2.x configs load unchanged
top.says: Upgrading needs no config changes; 2.x config files load as they are.
top.evidence: No test loads a 2.x config, so nothing in the repo confirms or refutes it.
top.fix: Add a test that loads the 2.x sample configs, or narrow the sentence to what has been tried.
top.where: Flagged to the fernway maintainers; the docs PR leaves the sentence until a test settles it.

footer: Fernway is a fictional library. This page is the worked example for the visual-inventory skill, rendered from `example.json`.
